sentences.text: Jabalisaurus tethyensis was a marine reptile belonging to the ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs, a group of highly adapted swimmers.
The genus comprises two species, J. meztli and J. tethyensis.
One specimen, catalogued as JME-SOS-08369, preserves a complete articulated skeleton together with soft tissue, and it had originally been assigned to Aegirosaurus sp. in 2022.
The type locality of J. tethyensis is the Altmühltal Formation in Germany.
The genus Jabalisaurus was erected by Barrientos-Lara and Alvarado-Ortega in 2021.

It is placed in the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae within the family Ophthalmosauridae, which belongs to the class Reptilia, and its known temporal range extends back to the Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago).
J. tethyensis lived during the Late Jurassic Tithonian stage.
The genus is recorded from Late Jurassic deposits in both Mexico and Germany.
